ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Helen Keller Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit to establish care after a fall at home. Concerns: Fell on her back steps three weeks ago where the handrail stops one step short; no injury, but she wants to keep walking outdoors and traveling for her work; Wants her visits conducted directly with her through a qualified tactile interpreter, with enough time and with written materials in braille; Wants a plan so that her way of communicating is respected if she is ever in hospital. [S]

tr.td: New patient visit to establish care after a fall at home
Two-week fall-risk and bone density review, and geriatric medicine consultation
Three-month falls prevention and function review
Six-month falls prevention and function review
Same-day sick visit for urinary symptoms
Fall evaluation by CDC STEADI: fall history, Timed Up and Go, 30-second chair stand, four-stage balance test, orthostatic blood pressure, medication review, feet and footwear, and vitamin D
Home strength and balance exercise with a physical therapist twice a week for 12 weeks, then daily on her own, with a qualified tactile interpreter at the therapy sessions
Geriatric medicine consultation for a comprehensive geriatric assessment adapted for deafblindness, including fall risk, cognition, and future care planning

Communication access: the clinic books and pays for a qualified tactile interpreter for every visit, she chooses the method, staff do not rely on her assistant to interpret, appointments are double length, and all documents are given in braille and accessible electronic text
Occupational therapy home safety visit: handrails on both sides, tactile edge strips on steps, clear routes, vibrating smoke and carbon monoxide alarms with a bed shaker, and a wearable alert button
Bone density screening by DXA, with FRAX risk, dietary calcium and vitamin D advice, and treatment only if risk reaches the treatment threshold
Protect touch and skin: check hand and foot sensation, skin, and the artificial eye socket at each preventive visit, and see the ocularist yearly to polish the prosthesis
No further falls, and a 30-second chair stand of 12 or more by the six-month review
No falls in six months; chair stand 12
Home changes complete: handrails on both sides of every step, tactile edge strips, and vibrating smoke and carbon monoxide alarms with a bed shaker
All installed after the occupational therapy home visit

A communication access plan in her chart: a qualified tactile interpreter booked by the clinic for every visit, double-length appointments, braille after-visit summaries, and a hospital communication passport
Plan recorded and passport written in braille and print
Keep traveling to speak, with a travel plan for falls and illness
Two speaking trips completed with a sighted guide

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; her assistant helps with driving, shopping, and print mail; moves through her home by touch along walls and rails, and outdoors with a sighted guide [S]
At intake: Timed Up and Go 13.5 seconds, 30-second chair stand 9, and tandem stance held 6 seconds, below the norms for her age [S]
By the six-month review: Timed Up and Go 11.2 seconds, chair stand 12, tandem stance 10 seconds; no further falls [S]
Alert, warm, witty, and precise; speech clear to those who know her and understandable with attention; follows rapid fingerspelling easily [S]
Mood good; PHQ-9 score 2 completed in braille; cognition intact on a tactile interview (see the consultation) [S]
